newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arianespace sets up finance company.
newsitem.headline: Arianespace sets up finance company.

text.p: The heavy satellite launch company Arianespace has set up a finance company to help it clients pay for launches aboard its rockets, the company said Wednesday.
The company said in a statement that Arianespace Finance, had been incorporated in Luxembourg and will provide $400 million in loans to Arianespace customers.

"The loans are principally for customers who do not yet have access to bank financing, because their projects are new and because they wish to finance their projects based on revenues generated by the satellite," the statement said.

"This financial instrument, designed to foster the development of new projects using the Ariane launcher, is available from the moment the launch services contract is signed. Coming into effect from the outset of the project, it gives customers fast, flexible assistance in structuring their overall financing plan," it said.
The loans will be refinanced by a group of banks including France's Credit Lyonnais, Chase Manhattan and Germany's Kreditanstalt fur Wiederaufbau.
The Paris-based Arianepace company launches the Ariane-4 rocket series from the European Space Agency (ESA) launch centre in French Guiana.
It leads the satellite launch market with firm orders to launch 42 heavy satellites worth an estimated $4.1 billion representing over 50 percent of the world market.

The company's plan to gradually replace by the year 2000 Ariane-4 rockets with the more powerful new-generation Ariane-5 rocket has been delayed for at least a year in the aftermath of the in-flight explosion of the first Ariane-5 rocket during its maiden flight on June 4.
Arianespace President Charles Bigot said last week that his company will make an order for more flight-proven Ariane-4 rockets to guarantee launch services for customers.
